To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a new model for workflow management systems based on Hoare logic that allows to: a. automatically check the correctness of workflows, b. automatically generate workflows, (2) the proposed model can be used to automatically check the correctness or automatically generate a workflow implementation that satisfies a given specification.

(1) we propose a new model of workflows and a new set of inference rules formalizing the semantics of the most common workflow constructs, (2) we provide a sound and complete proof system for workflow correctness, and (3) we provide a set algorithms for automatically checking if the workflow implementation respects its specification and for synthesizing a correct implementation from a workflow specification

(1) we formalized the semantics of workflows in terms of Hoare logic and we provided inference rules for each workflow construct, (2) we provided a formal framework for automatically checking the soundness of workflows and for automatically synthesizing workflows, (3) we provided a set of sound and complete inference rules for the existential and universal constructs that are new in workflow literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What does it mean that a workflow is implemented correctly?
(1) the formal semantics of workflows, (2) workflow verification, (3) workflow synthesis.
(1) providing a formal semantics for workflows and (2) using the formal semantics to provide automatic verification and generation of workflows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach provides a formal basis for automatic correctness checking of workflows and for the automatic synthesis of workflow implementations from their specifications and a given set of tasks.
the proposed model is a very good basis for the development of workflow systems.
we have provided a formal framework for specifying workflows and tasks and a set of algorithms for verifying and generating workflows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a formal semantics to workflows, we provide algorithms to check the correctness of workflows, and we provide algorithms for automatically generating workflows.
we have formalized workflow semantics, we have formalized a set of sound and complete inference rules, and we have provided algorithms for automatically checking and generating workflows.
we have developed a new formalism for specifying workflows and tasks and a set of algorithms for automatically checking and synthesizing workflows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the workflow verification problem is decidable and can be solved in polynomial time.
the correctness of a workflow is a matter of the correctness of the workflow implementation and the correctness of the tasks used to implement the workflow.
we provide a formal framework for the automatic verification and generation of workflow systems.
